evidence.claim: The New Mexico Tourism Department presents the Abbott-to-Logan drive through its grasslands, mission churches and state parks.
evidence.quote: Running southeast from Abbott to Logan, this scenic New Mexico route takes visitors past mission churches, through state parks and national grasslands.

evidence.claim: Shortgrass prairie is the dominant vegetation in the Kiowa and adjoining Rita Blanca grasslands, while the Canadian River cuts through the western unit.
evidence.quote: Semi-arid steppe grassland (shortgrass prairie) is the most common vegetation, covering 79 percent of the Grassland (including the adjacent Rita Blanca National Grassland).

evidence.claim: the Canadian River cuts through the western unit
evidence.quote: A few stands of Ponderosa Pine are found in the Canadian River Canyon in the western sector.

evidence.claim: the Canadian River cuts through the western unit
evidence.quote: The western unit is located in northwestern Harding, eastern Mora, and southeastern Colfax counties.

evidence.claim: The grassland mixes public and private land, and nearly all Kiowa National Grassland acreage is leased for cattle grazing.
evidence.quote: Nearly all of the land in the Kiowa National Grassland is leased to ranchers for grazing cattle

evidence.claim: The grassland mixes public and private land
evidence.quote: Both units of the National Grassland consist of a patchwork quilt of public land interspaced with private land.

evidence.claim: The corridor’s towns took shape with another transport route: the Dawson Railway, built through Roy in 1902 to carry the line from Tucumcari toward Dawson’s coal fields.
evidence.quote: It was relocated after the Dawson Railway was built from Tucumcari through the area in 1902, on its way to coal fields at Dawson.

evidence.claim: Roy moved to meet it, and Mosquero began as a railway water stop.
evidence.quote: The site was a water stop along the Dawson Railway, built in 1902 from Tucumcari to Dawson.

evidence.claim: After the rails were removed, Roy’s economy declined.
evidence.quote: The railroad was removed after 1950. This led to a significant decline in economic activity in Roy

evidence.claim: Solano, once Harding County’s largest town, also lost importance when Dawson’s coal mines closed in the 1950s.
evidence.quote: Solano was the largest town in Harding County for a time, and even published a local newspaper, The Solano Herald, but when the coal mines in Dawson shut down in the 1950s, its importance waned.

evidence.claim: At Mills, a separate excursion leads west to the Canadian River’s canyon rim.
evidence.quote: The rim of the Canadian River Canyon, also called Mills Canyon, is six miles (9.7 km) west of the nearly-deserted community of Mills.

evidence.claim: Continue through Roy, Solano and Mosquero; mission churches mark the stretch from Solano to Gallegos.
evidence.quote: It lies along NM 39 and the tracks of a spur of the Southern Pacific Railroad about half-way between Roy and Mosquero.

evidence.claim: mission churches mark the stretch from Solano to Gallegos
evidence.quote: Like a string of pearls, they stretch from Solano to Gallegos.

evidence.claim: The drive ends at Logan beside the Canadian River country of Ute Lake State Park.
evidence.quote: The byway ends in Logan, best known for Ute Lake State Park on the Canadian River

evidence.claim: Mills itself lies eleven miles north of Roy on NM 39.
evidence.quote: It lies on NM 39, eleven miles north of Roy.

evidence.claim: Six miles west of Mills, the Canadian River Canyon opens 700 feet deep and more than a mile across.
evidence.quote: The canyon is 700 feet (210 m) deep and more than 1 mi (1.6 km) wide from rim to rim.

evidence.claim: Its red rock and vegetation belong to the western unit of New Mexico’s Kiowa National Grassland.
evidence.quote: About 15 mi (24 km) of the red-rock, well-vegetated canyon are in the National Grassland.

evidence.claim: On the canyon floor, ruins mark Melvin Mills’s early-1900s homestead, where he had a home and apple orchard.
evidence.quote: On the canyon floor are the ruins of the homestead of Melvin Mills who had an apple orchard and a home here in the early 1900s.

evidence.claim: The community above takes its name from Mills, a rancher and attorney.
evidence.quote: Mills was named after Melvin W. Mills, a rancher and attorney.

evidence.claim: A primitive campground occupies the rim; the road below accommodates walkers, horses and high-clearance vehicles.
evidence.quote: A primitive campground is on the rim.  A road down into the canyon is traversable by foot, horseback, or high-clearance vehicles.

evidence.claim: The road into the canyon calls for a high-clearance vehicle.

evidence.quote: The village's historical size can be seen in the more than 40 city blocks that make up Roy.

evidence.quote: The village, originally 2 miles (3.2 km) west of its current site, was founded by ranchers Frank and William Roy, and named for Frank as the first postmaster in 1901.
